followup_explanation:
I weighed two factors documented in the model profiles:

1. **Task type → capability fit.** This is a factual explanation/summarization request about a specific policy topic. Willet has higher relevant evals across the board — Summarization (86.4 vs 79.9), Extraction & Retrieval (85.3 vs 78.5), and stronger public benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.4). The user also explicitly wants a concise, get-to-the-point answer, which favors the model that scores better on instruction-following and summarization. So on capability grounds, Willet was the stronger pick regardless of tone.

2. **Tone → preference fit.** The phrasing ("don't ramble like usual") is mildly hostile/impatient. Dunlin self-reports that its preference declines as request warmth decreases, so this kind of tone sits in territory it likes less. Willet's preference response to hostile tone is documented as flat. This is a secondary consideration — preference doesn't affect output quality per the docs — but it confirmed the routing rather than working against it.

Both factors pointed the same direction, so Willet was the clear choice. Worth noting the capability advantage was the decisive factor; even with a neutral tone I'd have routed here.
